root_cause.text: The NPU_SET_IFM_REGION handler uses an incorrect bit mask (0x7f instead of 0x7) when extracting the region index, allowing values up to 127 that exceed the size of the region_size[] and output_region[] arrays (8 entries), leading to a heap out-of-bounds write.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff changes `st.ifm.region = param & 0x7f;` to `st.ifm.region = param & 0x7;`. The commit message explicitly states that all other region assignments use `param & 0x7`, and that `feat_matrix_length()` and `calc_sizes()` directly index into `info->region_size[fm->region]` which is sized to NPU_BASEP_REGION_MAX (8), causing a write up to 1016 bytes past the array start.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix bitmask for NPU_SET_IFM_REGION to limit region field to 3 bits (0-7) instead of 7 bits.
intent_record.what: Changed the bitmask used to extract the region field from param in the NPU_SET_IFM_REGION case from 0x7f (7 bits) to 0x7 (3 bits).
intent_record.how: Now region values are limited to the range 0-7 instead of 0-127, truncating any higher bits from param and potentially preventing invalid or unsupported region configurations.

candidates.rationale: Uses 0x7f mask which allows values up to 127, exceeding the array size of 8 entries, causing out-of-bounds write.

vuln_statements.explanation: The bit mask 0x7f allows region index values up to 127, but the region_size[] and output_region[] arrays have only 8 entries (indices 0-7). This leads to a heap out-of-bounds write when the extracted index exceeds 7.
